title: Session Surge Economics & Instrumentation — One-pager (draft)
body:
TL;DR
This one-pager summarizes a small benchmarking sweep intended to (1) quantify dollar impact of short session surges (microbursts) under current fastpath + batcher config, and (2) propose lightweight instrumentation hooks to make per-session surge economics observable in the Console. Result: microbursts (~100–500 qps for 6–12s) increase effective $/k-token by 18–45% depending on prewarm policy and KV cache hit distribution.

Motivation and scope
- Problem: product teams see intermittent p99 spikes that blow past SLOs and inflate unit cost, but current dashboards only show aggregated server-side token cost and latency percentiles.
- Goal: produce a minimal set of actionable metrics + a short econ vignette that explains why transient surges inflate per-query spend and how small instrumentation additions reduce MTTD and optimization friction.
- Scope: hosted API surface, service-tier = standard fastpath (no Dedicated). Model variants: medium-sized LLM (redwood-m-7b-like) and a compact quantized variant (redwood-m-7b-q4).

Experiment setup (repro notes)
- Hardware: GPU pool type g4dn-like (16GB) simulated on local infra harness; bucketed throughput injection to mimic client-side surge patterns.
- Model sizes: base (fp16) and quant (q4_0).
- Warm states: 3 prewarm policies tested: none (cold-on-demand), soft-prewarm (keep 1 slot warm for 30s idle), aggressive-prewarm (keep 2 slots warm).
- KV cache: synthetic hit-rates: low (5%), med (25%), high (60%) — hits concentrated on first-turn tokens (prefix-heavy).
- Load pattern: steady 50 qps baseline, test microburst windows of 100–500 qps for 6, 12, 30 seconds. Each scenario repeated 3x, captured 120s total traces.

Key numeric summar y (excerpt)
- Chart notes: these are ASCII summaries of the observed averages across runs. Costs normalized to baseline steady-50 qps (baseline $/1000tokens = 1.00).

Scenario matrix (selected rows):
+------------------------------------------+--------+--------+--------+
| Scenario                                 | p50 ms| p99 ms | $/k t |
+------------------------------------------+--------+--------+--------+
| Baseline steady 50 qps (med KV)          | 120   | 240   | 1.00  |
| Microburst 200 qps x12s (no prewarm)     | 160   | 520   | 1.38  |
| Microburst 200 qps x12s (soft-prewarm)   | 140   | 380   | 1.22  |
| Microburst 500 qps x6s (no prewarm)      | 210   | 920   | 1.45  |
| Microburst 500 qps x6s (aggr-prewarm)    | 155   | 420   | 1.18  |
| Microburst 200 qps x12s (high KV)        | 130   | 300   | 1.08  |
| Microburst 200 qps x12s (low KV)         | 180   | 740   | 1.62  |
+------------------------------------------+--------+--------+--------+

Observations (short)
- Short surges amplify tail latency disproportionately: p99 increases >3x for some no-prewarm cases because of queueing + decode contention.
- Dollar impact correlates with wasted slot-time: when many requests wait for slot allocation, the amortized token throughput per GPU drops.
- Prewarm reduces both latency tail and $/k, but has a baseline cost (kept-warm slots). Aggressive prewarm pays off for frequent microbursts (>4 per minute) but not for rare events.
- KV cache hit-rate significantly dampens microburst penalty (high KV => closer to baseline). For prefix-heavy workloads, small caching improvements yield outsized savings.

Instrumentation proposal (minimal, developer-friendly)
- New per-session counters/tags to emit (Console + traces):
  - session.surge_flag (bool) -> true if session sees >N qps over T seconds (configurable),
  - session.peak_qps (int), session.surge_duration_s (int), session.kv_hitrate (pct),
  - session.slot_wait_ms_total, session.slot_active_ms_total, session.queued_calls_total.
- Aggregation rollups in Console:
  - surge cohort page: group sessions by surge flag and show p50/p90/p99 + $/k-token for cohort vs baseline,
  - "slot efficiency" metric: active_ms / (active_ms + wait_ms) per cohort.
- Lightweight export: encode new counters as fields in existing request-level trace proto so no schema churn; provide an opt-in sampling rate (default 0.5%) for high-traffic tenants.

Small ascii visualization (cohort econ snapshot)
- Baseline cohort: avg $/k = 1.00, slot_eff = 0.82, p99 = 240ms
- Surge cohort (200 qps x12s): avg $/k = 1.38, slot_eff = 0.56, p99 = 520ms

Operational recommendations
1) Implement the instrumentation (above) behind an experiment flag and wire basic rollups to Console telemetry. Target: 2-week rollout to collect representative cohorts.
2) Add a "surge detector" alert (Console) that triggers when session.surge_rate > threshold *and* slot_eff drops below 0.6 — this should cut MTTD for transient microbursts.
3) Tune default prewarm heuristics: consider adaptive prewarm that keeps 1 slot idle for tenants with observed surge-rate > 2/min (use the new metrics to qualify).
4) Surface a developer-side "surge cost estimate" in SDK docs (so app devs can reason about client-side batching/backoff).

Risks and open questions
- Sampling cost vs value: default 0.5% trace sampling should be validated; heavy tenants might need lower sampling. What SLA/privacy concerns from customers? (cc security/compliance)
- Accuracy of simulated KV distribution vs real product traffic — we need a 48h production trace pull (anonymized) to validate assumed hit-rates. Linked INF ticket above.
- Prewarm sizing: what's the real cost of keeping 1 slot warm globally during low-traffic windows for RU? Need finance model to compute break-even cadence.

Next steps (first 30 days)
- (A) Instrumentation PR: telemetry + trace proto change (small) — owner: Lukas. Target: feature-flagged PR in 1 week.
- (B) Console rollup mock: basic surge cohort chart + slot_eff metric prototype — owner: me (Aisha). Mock by day 10.
- (C) Run a production sample using 0.2% sampling for 48 hours to validate KV hit assumptions — owner: Priya.
- (D) Finance sanity check for prewarm break-even — owner: Jonah (cc finance).

Notes to self / friction points
- Keep the instrumentation payload tiny (5 fields) to avoid telemetry bloat.
- Slack thread: #observability-burst for quick sync.
- Link to existing runtime prewarm knobs: runtime/docs/prewarm-policy.md (PR forthcoming).

Appendix: quick run-book for reproducing the bench locally
1) checkout runtime perf-harness branch: perf/surge-instr (PR linked above).
2) run harness with --burst-pattern=200:12, --kv-profile=med, --prewarm=soft --repeat=3 --trace-out=surge-trace.json
3) ingestion helper: tools/ingest-traces --file surge-trace.json --target console-dev --flag enable-surge-fields

End of one-pager. Feedback welcome — particularly on (a) suggested minimal sampling defaults, (b) slot_eff formula, and (c) how to expose surge-cost-estimate to SDKs without scaring users.
